issues.legal_issue: A person in settled possession may obtain protection against interference even when that person has not proved title and the alleged owner has not established a better title.
material_facts: The plaintiff failed to prove title to the disputed land but was found to be in settled possession of it.
The defendant also failed to prove title to the disputed land.
The defendant obstructed the plaintiff’s use of the land, and the courts below restrained interference with the plaintiff’s possession.
issues.conclusion: The injunction protecting the plaintiff’s possession was properly granted, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Indian law, peaceful and settled possession is protected against forcible interference, even by the true owner; a person claiming a better right must obtain possession through due process. Settled possession must be effective and undisturbed, known to the owner or not concealed, and the dispossession of the owner must be complete and acquiesced in; casual or stray trespass does not suffice. The Court relied on Midnapur Zamindary Co. Ltd. v. Kumar Naresh Narayan Roy, Lallu Yeshwant Singh v. Rao Jagdish Singh, Nair Service Society Ltd. v. K.C. Alexander, M.C. Chockalingam v. V. Manickavasagam, Krishna Ram Mahale v. Shobha Venkat Rao, Nagar Palika, Jind v. Jagat Singh, Munshi Ram v. Delhi Administration, Puran Singh v. State of Punjab, Ram Rattan v. State of Uttar Pradesh, and Ramesh Chand Ardawatiya v. Anil Panjwani. No statutory provision was relied on.

rule.if: civil_possessory_injunction_appeal and plaintiff_in_settled_possession and plaintiff_title_unproved and defendant_interference_threatened and defendant_better_title_unproved

predicates.civil_possessory_injunction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an injunction sought to protect possession of property.
predicates.plaintiff_in_settled_possession: The plaintiff had effective, undisturbed possession of the property that was not concealed from the owner.
predicates.plaintiff_title_unproved: The plaintiff did not establish title to the property.
predicates.defendant_interference_threatened: The defendant threatened or attempted to interfere with the plaintiff’s possession.
predicates.defendant_better_title_unproved: The defendant did not establish a better title entitling the defendant to possession.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a possessory injunction and the plaintiff was in settled possession, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant proved title, and interference was threatened, the possession is protected by an injunction.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking only an injunction may be maintained when the plaintiff proves possession and faces invasion by a person who has not established title, even though title is disputed.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought relief based on both alleged title and possession but did not prove title.
The trial court found that the plaintiff had proved possession and that the defendant had not proved title to the disputed land.
The trial court left title undecided and granted an injunction against interference with possession.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a claim for declaration of title did not make the suit for injunction unmaintainable.
issues.legal_principle: A person seeking an injunction need not prove title if that person proves lawful possession and that possession is invaded or threatened by a person who has no established title. Where title is unclear but possession is established and was not obtained by unfair means shortly before suit, title may be left open while possessory relief is granted. The Court agreed with Fakirbhai Bhagwandas v. Maganlal Haribhai and the stated position in Kallappa Rama Londa v. Shivappa Nagappa Aparaj; it distinguished Sri Dasnam Naga Sanyasi v. Allahabad Development Authority. No statutory provision was relied on.

rule.if: injunction_only_suit and plaintiff_possession_proved and title_disputed and interference_by_unproven_claimant

predicates.injunction_only_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking an injunction without seeking a declaration of title.
predicates.plaintiff_possession_proved: The plaintiff proved possession of the property.
predicates.title_disputed: The parties disputed who held title to the property.
predicates.interference_by_unproven_claimant: A person who had not established title threatened or attempted to invade the plaintiff’s possession.

issues.definition: A suit seeking only an injunction is maintainable when the plaintiff proves possession, title is disputed, and a person without established title threatens or attempts interference.

issues.legal_issue: A judgment granting an injunction on the basis of possession without deciding title leaves the parties’ title claims open for later adjudication.
material_facts: The trial court decided the suit on possession after finding that neither party had established title.
The High Court upheld the injunction, and the Supreme Court clarified that the judgment did not decide title for or against either party.
issues.conclusion: The judgment did not determine title, and either party remained free to establish title in properly constituted proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: A possessory injunction may be granted while the question of title is expressly left open; such a judgment is not an adjudication of title. The Court distinguished the title question from the possessory relief and confirmed that the parties could pursue their respective title claims in separate legal proceedings. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this clarification.

predicates.possession_based_injunction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an injunction granted on the basis of possession.
predicates.title_issue_left_open: The court granting the injunction did not decide which party held title to the property.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an injunction based on possession and the title issue was left undecided, the parties’ title claims remain open for separate proceedings.
